title: Leaky tenant burst credit fallback causing cascading 429s across Dedicated and Private customers
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Several Dedicated and Private customers started seeing sustained 429s during the 2026-03-09 maintenance window and again on 2026-03-10 after a leader failover in the rate-limiter service. The symptoms were cascading tenant lockouts and burst credits that never recovered, even after normal traffic subsided.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed):
- A race in burst-credit fallback logic during cluster leader transitions allowed a path where a tenant's burst token balance could be decremented below zero and persisted.
- The reconciliation path that should have corrected negative balances was disabled for tenants pinned to Dedicated pools to avoid cross-pool noise. That combination meant negative balances persisted and caused continuous reject (429) responses for affected tenants.
- An unrelated optimization that memoized per-tenant quota windows in local memory caused stale windows to be written back to the DB on leader change, overwriting correct values with stale, negative balances.

Impact:
- Multiple paying Dedicated customers and a subset of Private on-prem clusters experienced partial or full outages for inference traffic over 3+ hours across two incidents.
- Engineering pager fired P0; Support escalated high-priority tickets and coordinated customer workarounds.

Immediate mitigation performed: 
1) Emergency config change: disabled fallbacks to the global shared-burst pool for affected Dedicated shards to prevent cross-tenant cascading credit depletion (admin change rolled at 02:15 UTC, 2026-03-10).
2) Manual resync: executed a targeted reconciliation script to clamp negative balances to zero for known impacted tenant IDs (script run and verified).
3) Canary rollback: reverted the recent memoization optimization on leader-handling branch and rolled to 10% of traffic for 2 hours before full rollback.

Permanent fix plan: 
- Patch: add atomic compare-and-set (CAS) when updating tenant burst tokens to prevent negative persistence; add server-side clamp and audit log when negative values observed.
- Re-enable and harden reconciliation for Dedicated pools with tenant-aware rate-limiter guards so reconciliation can run safely without cross-pool side effects.
- Add leader-transition unit/integration tests that simulate concurrent decrement + leader failover to catch regression.
- Migration: run a one-time background resync job in production to scan and repair anomalous balances across all pools (with safety throttles).
- Observability: add metrics for "negative_burst_balance_count", "fallback_to_global_pool_rate", and a reconciliation success/failure counter. Create an SLO alert for sustained 429 rate > 1% for > 5 minutes for Dedicated customers.

Rollout plan: 
- PR in staging (PR #12345) with CAS + clamps + tests. Run full integration in staging with synthetic workload that stresses leader swaps.
- Canary rollout to 5% of production traffic for 30 minutes; then 25% for 1 hour; then full rollout if no regressions.
- Schedule migration/resync during low-traffic maintenance window with support on-call present.

Postmortem and customer comms:
- Draft postmortem to be published to Confluence after incident blameless review. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/ENG-30521-postmortem (placeholder).
- Customer-facing notes drafted for Support to send to affected tenants summarizing root cause, mitigations, and compensatory actions.

Acceptance criteria:
- No tenant burst tokens can be persisted < 0 in production for > 1 minute.
- Reconciliation job runs without creating cross-pool credit transfers.
- Observability coverage and alerts in place and validated with synthetic failure injection.

Notes / constraints:
- Private/on-prem deployments require an opt-in agent update; plan an ops guide for Private customers to apply the fix (will require a minor version bump).
- Dedicated pool changes require coordination with capacity/ops to avoid noisy neighbor regressions during reconciliation.
